summary.text: Animated enhanced infrared (EIR) satellite imagery depicts a contracting eye, now measured at 31 NM, characterized by cooling eye temperatures (15C) and warming cloud-top temperatures within the central dense overcast (cdo). Typhoon (TY) 30W has begun its east- northeastward turn over the past six hours as the STR to the east shifts subtly southward and its northwestern boundary erodes in response to a mid-latitude shortwave trough passing to the north. Once the trough passes to the north in the next 6-12 hours, the STR to the west will strengthen and build eastward, while the ridge to the east weakens and shifts southward.

records.significantForecastChanges: THERE ARE NO SIGNIFICANT CHANGES TO THE FORECAST FROM THE PREVIOUS WARNING.

summary.text: Animated multispectral satellite imagery (MSI) depicts typhoon (TY) 30W (in-fa) with a cooling eye that has become partially cloud-filled and ragged. 30W has likely begun its clockwise loop as it stalls in track speed within the col between the subtropical ridges (strs) centered to the east and west of the system. By +48h, a passing mid- latitude trough will weaken the western STR and allow the eastern STR to regain primary steering influence, inducing a poleward turn by +60h and a northeastward turn by +72h.

summary.text: Typhoon (TY) 30W underwent significant consolidation between 0600Z and 1800Z, with a ring of -60 to -65 degrees Celsius cloud-top temperatures encircling a ragged 30-NM-wide eye. TY 30W has turned sharply poleward as it rounds the western periphery of the STR. The strong poleward outflow channel will become increasingly unable to overcome these detrimental environmental effects, but increasing baroclinic instability should offset some of the weakening.
